# dreamrouter_clients (Data Source)

Lists the devices (clients) on the network: those connected now, those seen within `days`, and blocked devices however long ago they were seen. Like leases, this describes the network right now (uptime, traffic and signal change constantly), so use it for lookups, e.g. finding a device's MAC address to block or reserve it, rather than feeding changing values into resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Connected devices, and devices seen in the last 7 days.
data "dreamrouter_clients" "all" {}

# Only Wi-Fi devices that are online now.
data "dreamrouter_clients" "wifi" {
  status          = "online"
  connection_type = "wifi"
}

# Blocked devices, however long ago they were seen.
data "dreamrouter_clients" "blocked" {
  blocked = true
}

locals {
  # Devices with a weak Wi-Fi signal, by name.
  weak_signal = { for c in data.dreamrouter_clients.wifi.clients : c.mac => c.name if c.signal < -75 }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `blocked` (Boolean) Only return blocked (true) or unblocked (false) devices.
- `connection_type` (String) Only return "wired" or "wifi" devices. Devices the router has only a stored record for (never connected, or not seen within days) have no connection and are left out.
- `days` (Number) How many days back to look for offline devices. Defaults to 7.
- `network` (String) Only return devices on the network with this name (case-insensitive).
- `status` (String) Only return devices that are "online" or "offline".

### Read-Only

- `clients` (Attributes List) Matching devices, sorted by IP address (devices without one last). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--clients))

<a id="nestedatt--clients"></a>
### Nested Schema for `clients`

Read-Only:

- `band` (String) Wi-Fi band: "2.4GHz", "5GHz" or "6GHz"; empty for wired devices.
- `blocked` (Boolean) Whether the device is blocked.
- `connection` (String) "wired" or "wifi"; empty if the device hasn't been seen recently.
- `dns_name` (String) The device's DNS name (see dreamrouter_host); empty if none.
- `download_bytes` (Number) Bytes the device has downloaded.
- `hostname` (String) The host name the device sent; may be empty.
- `ip` (String) The device's IP address: its current one, else its last one, else its reserved one; may be empty.
- `last_seen` (String) When the device was last seen, as an RFC 3339 timestamp (UTC); empty if never.
- `link_mbps` (Number) Link speed of a wired device in Mbit/s; 0 if unknown.
- `mac` (String) The device's MAC address, in lower-case colon form.
- `name` (String) The device's name: the one set in the web UI, else the router's name for it, else its host name; may be empty.
- `network_id` (String) ID of the network the device is on; may be empty.
- `note` (String) The note set on the device in the web UI; empty if none.
- `port` (Number) Switch or router port of a wired device; 0 if unknown.
- `reserved` (Boolean) Whether the device has a DHCP reservation.
- `signal` (Number) Wi-Fi signal strength in dBm (e.g. -61); 0 for wired or offline devices.
- `ssid` (String) Wi-Fi network name; empty for wired devices.
- `status` (String) "online" or "offline".
- `uplink` (String) The access point, switch or router the device connects through.
- `upload_bytes` (Number) Bytes the device has uploaded.
- `uptime` (Number) Seconds the device has been connected; 0 if offline.
- `vendor` (String) Manufacturer, from the MAC address; may be empty.
